title: Understand How Satellite Links Shape IoT Device Design and Testing
abstract: How 3GPP Releases 15, 16, and 17 brought satellite access into 5G NR, NB-IoT, and eMTC. Why satellite links suit IoT devices that send small, infrequent, and delay-tolerant messages. Where non-terrestrial networks (NTN) add value, including asset tracking, agriculture, public safety, and offshore operations. How power efficiency, RF signaling, and antenna design shape satellite-connected device development. Why long propagation delay, Doppler shift, and intermittent coverage make static test methods insufficient. Which measurements show deployment readiness, such as transmit power, modulation accuracy, spectral emissions, receiver sensitivity, and block error rate (BLER). title: MAHA PAC spent more on steak, luxury club than candidates, report shows
abstract: In the wake of the Make America Healthy Again movement's midterm wipeout , a top leader suggested the heavy losses came down to being outspent by wealthier, more powerful rivals. But a Stat report on MAHA's own spending in the run-up to the election raises questions about whether the group's priority was ever winning elections in the first place. The dive into the financial documents reveals that the MAHA PAC, led by Tony Lyons, spent more on allies, boosters, meals, luxuries, and its affiliated nonprofit than it did on political candidates. The findings are in stark contrast to an announcement from Lyons in the spring that he was heading a $100 million fundraiser to boost MAHA's clout in the midterms . In reality, MAHA PAC took in $3.2 million. During the election cycle, the PAC spent more than $10.5 million, with over $7 million coming from money it had collected previously. title: Man hired by Russia spied on Silicon Valley tech and defense company, feds say
abstract: A Russian national has been indicted on suspicions he was a Russian spy who stalked and surveilled employees of a Silicon Valley company that was assisting Ukraine in its ongoing war with its eastern neighbor. Igor D’iu, 25, allegedly photographed the employees and their computer screens as they worked at a coffee shop located near the company’s Palo Alto office, federal prosecutors said Wednesday . He also kept a list of home addresses of employees and a senior executive. At one point, prosecutors said, D’iu trailed an employee as she traveled home from Palo Alto to San Francisco. An affidavit filed in the case referred to the employee as FEMP1, short for female employee, and said the event left her “in a state of emotional distress.” Evasive and irregular turns “FEMP1 made evasive and irregular turns, took back roads, and turned into a grocery store parking lot where D’IU continued aggressively following her vehicle,” an FBI special agent wrote. “D’IU followed FEMP1 through U-turns, illegal left turns, and ran a red light to stay with FEMP1 for nearly thirty miles. FEMP1 called 911 while driving and was instructed to drive directly to San Francisco Police Department (“SFPD”) Mission Station. Near SFPD Mission Station, FEMP1 flagged an SFPD patrol vehicle and reported the incident. D’IU left once FEMP1 made contact with the patrol vehicle.” Read full article Comments

title: Traumatized teens sue school, cops after Doritos bag triggers AI gun alert
abstract: In October 2025, four Black high school students were sharing Cool Ranch Doritos after football practice, winding down and waiting for their rides home. It was then, in the lull of a moment any teen with after-school activities knows well, that the school’s AI gun detection system suddenly flagged one teen holding a bag of chips as a potential gunman. Within two minutes, Baltimore County Public Schools officials who reviewed security camera footage linked to the alert determined there was no actual threat. They recognized the Doritos bag and canceled the alert, which notified not only other school officials but also the Baltimore County Police Department that no response was needed. The false alert could have ended there—before a traumatizing campus clash with police—but it didn’t. Read full article Comments

title: Google turns to Blue Origin for a rocket, but its long-term problem remains
abstract: Blue Origin announced Thursday that its New Glenn rocket will launch data center satellites for Google in 2029 as part of that company's Project Suncatcher program. Google disclosed it was working on scalable orbiting data centers about a year ago and characterized the project as one of its research "moonshots." The mission on New Glenn is designed to deploy satellites, each with computing capacity at roughly the scale of a data center rack, into Sun-synchronous orbit where they can receive nearly continuous solar energy. "Project Suncatcher is a long-term moonshot to scale AI infrastructure in space by tapping into the abundant solar power in orbit," said Travis Beals, senior director of Project Suncatcher at Google, in the news release. "This dedicated launch with Blue Origin represents a crucial milestone on our roadmap as we expand the boundaries of what's possible for the future of compute." Read full article Comments

title: "You’re right"—LLMs will get climate info wrong if you ask
abstract: Many studies over the years have examined how people encounter climate science information. Some focused on the top results that Google surfaced (back when Google was still in the business of serving links), while others examined social media content or newspaper and TV news coverage. With large language models (LLMs) now forming a share of the public information diet, it's worth looking at how they handle climate change. But there’s no direct way for researchers to look at the information people have seen. It is served ephemerally to individual users, confined to their chat session. A study led by researchers from University College London and the United Nations Educational, Scientific, and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) tried to tackle this question from multiple angles, testing LLMs with different prompts and evaluating their output. They started with benchmarks of simple factual questions (benchmarks that might even be in models’ training data at this point) but also analyzed more complex interactions—including when users think they’re right to push back on an answer. CO 2 Q&A LLM research often faces ( no-true-Scotsman-tinged ) criticism for focusing on a particular model rather than some other frontier model that may have been released after the experiment concluded. In this case, the study used 33 models, including multiple versions of the major frontier and open-weight models. The flagship frontier models used were Claude Fable 5, Claude Opus 5, Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview, Gemini 3.6 Flash, and GPT-5.6 Sol. (You can find the full list in the report .) Read full article Comments

title: Google will launch Android app verification requirement globally in January 2027
abstract: Google announced Android developer verification last year , and despite numerous objections from developers and users, the company is forging ahead . It began blocking the installation of unregistered apps in some countries this fall, and the system is expanding globally soon. Google says it will start rolling out the requirement in all regions in January 2027, and it urges devs who still haven't registered their apps to do so soon. The apps you download from the Play Store all come from verified developers, and Google's new requirement expands that requirement to apps from third-party sources. Once developer verification is live in your region, you won't be able to sideload apps unless the developer has registered with Google, which is framed as a security measure . Verification requires providing government identification and paying a $25 fee, which will allegedly make it harder for nefarious actors to distribute malware and scammy apps. In September, Google launched verification in Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore, and Thailand. Apparently, nothing exploded, so the company is now ready to expand. It previously said verification would go global in 2027, and it's not wasting any time with the January start. It says that verification will reach all devices within "several months." title: Mouse fight club might explain why we like to watch violent things
abstract: Credit: J.M. Iravedra-Garcia et al., 2026 Credit: J.M. Iravedra-Garcia et al., 2026 There's something about watching violent events that broadly appeals to us, whether it's the latest John Wick movie, a video game, or a live UFC bout. Scientists have debated whether watching violent things could make us more aggressive, but it could also be an adaptive survival strategy. Male mice, for instance, who watched other mice fighting learned enough about how to fight to better protect themselves (compared to mice who didn't watch fights) when pitted against stronger, more aggressive opponents, according to a paper published in the journal Nature. The team randomly assigned male mice to three groups—fighters, spectators, or novices—and then subjected each group to eight days of training with three 10-minute sessions per day. The novices played with stuffed mice in isolation, while the spectators watched various pairs of fighter mice battle from a raised platform behind a transparent barrier—a set-up chosen to let them smell and listen to the fights as well as observe them. The ninth day was "fight night," when all the mice had to face a daunting opponent in three 4-minute rounds. Each fight was filmed from above so that the mouse behavior could be analyzed. To monitor corresponding changes in brain activity, the team engineered the rodents' excitatory brain cells to glow green whenever they were activated, while inhibitory brain cells glowed red. They also implanted tiny optical fibers into 12 interconnected brain regions so they could track changing activity in every brain region simultaneously. Read full article Comments

title: NASA's new Moon plans have a problem: Orion wasn't designed to fly this way
abstract: NASA recently announced a significant shakeup to the Artemis program that will land humans on the Moon. The moves were designed to give the agency's lunar lander providers—SpaceX with its Starship vehicle, and Blue Origin with Blue Moon—more flexibility in reaching the Moon. For Starship, this means docking with Orion in Earth orbit, and then traveling to the Moon in tandem. For Blue Moon, it shifts the rendezvous with Orion all the way to low-lunar orbit. These changes benefit the lunar landers, but in turn impose more of a burden on the Orion spacecraft, which is built for NASA by Lockheed Martin. To understand the implications for the spacecraft, Ars spoke with Kirk Shireman, Human Spaceflight Exploration and Orion program manager at Lockheed. Read full article Comments

title: How to tell a cyberattack from a plain old outage
abstract: Over the past week, anyone could be forgiven for wondering whether a Diehard IV –style cyberwar had finally arrived in the US. Across just four consecutive business days, a mass Microsoft exchange outage broke IT services for thousands of companies , a Federal Aviation Administration tech screw-up grounded airplanes across the country, a software problem affecting JPMorgan Chase caused another round of disruption, a United Airlines system glitch delayed flights yet again, and an NSA classified network’s downtime left the agency’s staff sitting at home waiting to return to their office at Fort Meade. In the midst of a US war with Iran and rising fears of AI-enabled hacking , this still-unfolding comedy of IT errors colliding across American infrastructure felt to plenty of observers like more than a coincidence. Yet there’s still no evidence that any one of these clustered technological failures were related, much less caused by hackers. Their improbable, sequential timing left Americans anxiously doomscrolling for signs of foul play. But in cases like these, it’s the job of cybersecurity analysts (and reporters at WIRED) to determine—vibes aside—whether the latest tech outage was actually an accident or the result of a cyberattack. Read full article Comments

title: Ted Cruz-led committee approves Trump FCC nominee 15-0 as Democrats boycott vote
abstract: A Senate committee chaired by Ted Cruz (R-Texas) voted today to approve a Federal Communications Commission nominee, despite accusations that the nominee gave false testimony about her work as a legal advisor for FCC Chairman Brendan Carr. Democrats attempted to prevent a quorum by not showing up, but Cruz proceeded with a Republican-only vote. All 15 Republicans on the Senate Commerce Committee voted to approve Trump nominee Danielle Thumann, while the committee's 13 Democrats were absent. "We're going to be doing our job today, even if the Democrats refuse to show up to do theirs," Cruz said at today's hearing. Nominees are vetted in committees first, and then require majority approval from the Senate. Republicans are hoping to get Thumann confirmed before Democrats take Senate control in January. title: Ukraine blew up Putin’s bridge using relay drones to bypass Starlink limits
abstract: A Ukrainian barrage of missiles and drones collapsed a crucial segment of Russian President Vladimir Putin’s prized Kerch Strait Bridge—and Ukraine’s military pulled off the strike deep within Russian-occupied territory without relying on the military-grade version of Elon Musk’s Starlink satellite communications to guide the missiles in. On the nights of November 15 and November 16, coordinated waves of Ukrainian drones and missiles caused enough damage to collapse one of two steel arches supporting the Kerch bridge’s roadway for automobile traffic, according to an Institute for the Study of War update . Russian sources claimed several hundred Ukrainian drones first overwhelmed Russian air defenses to pave the way for remote-controlled missile strikes focused on the bridge, with the latter prominently including Ukraine’s homegrown Flamingo cruise missile. The Ukrainian operation adapted a Russian battlefield innovation by using drones equipped with mesh radios to create an airborne communications network, according to the Financial Times . Each networked drone acts as a relay node to extend the communication link between human operators and remotely piloted missiles and strike drones. Russia began using the technique to support long-range drone and missile strikes on Ukrainian cities. Read full article Comments

title: Trump abandons his FDA nominee, and Senate scraps vote on his NSF pick
abstract: In the span of less than 24 hours, two Trump administration nominees have suffered sudden blows—Trump's pick to lead the Food and Drug Administration and his pick to lead the National Science Foundation. Late Tuesday evening, Axios reported that the White House had abruptly withdrawn its controversial nomination of Heidi Overton to lead the FDA. Overton, a top conservative domestic policy aide in the White House, has drawn criticism and skepticism from Republicans and Democrats alike over her stances on vaccines, abortion, vapes, and birth control. Overton opposes abortion—though perhaps not strongly enough for some Republicans—and supported Trump and Kennedy's decried anti-vaccine policies and statements, vexing Democrats. In her confirmation hearing in September, Overton consistently stonewalled senators on every topic, refusing to directly answer even softball questions from friendly Republicans, leaving lawmakers on both sides of the aisle openly frustrated. The questions she dodged included those on how she would handle the FDA's current safety review of the abortion pill, mifepristone, which extensive data has established is extremely safe. She also wouldn't say whether she agreed with Trump when he falsely claimed the measles vaccine is "quite lethal" or that children are given vaccine doses the "size of a soda bottle." Overton repeatedly refused to answer whether Trump could ever be wrong. Read full article Comments

title: Netflix CEO admits app may bury stuff you want to watch under stuff you don’t
abstract: The streaming wars, or the battle to be the top streaming company, are ongoing, according to Ted Sarandos, a co-CEO of what many would consider today’s frontrunner. When it comes to subscribers, no streaming service has more than Netflix, which reported having over 325 million subscribers as of January. But in an interview with Bloomberg published today, Sarandos noted that people are still spending significant time watching traditional broadcast TV. Read full article Comments

title: Windows Server 2028 trades compatibility for out-of-the-box security
abstract: Microsoft's Ignite announcements this week went beyond the Office-in-Copilot overhaul with the reveal of the Windows Server 2028 Public Preview and its new security-by-default stance and what Microsoft calls Hardened Server Core . Windows Server 2028 will implement a default security framework that Microsoft says is aligned with hardened DoD benchmarks, such as the Defense Information Systems Agency's (DISA) Security Technical Implementation Guide (STIG). STIGs work by providing a standard security framework for system administrators to follow recommended guidance. In the past, Windows Server admins were left to start from a blank canvas and then implement hardening configurations for operations. Secure baselines were available but not the default. Microsoft says that concern is now managed: "The s ecure configuration is the starting state, not a project you run after setup. That closes the window where a newly deployed server sits exposed while it waits to be hardened. " The new Windows Server 2028 hardened-by-default state will only be available for the Server Core installs. Windows Server Desktop Experience installs do not include the changed stance. Read full article Comments

abstract: Best Buy is selling Blu-rays directly through its website and in physical stores again after exiting Blu-ray and DVD sales in 2023. The Best Buy website’s movie section currently lists 15 Blu-rays (including one two-pack) that are “sold & shipped by Best Buy.” New titles available include The Odyssey (2026), Project Hail Mary (2026), Supergirl (2026), Super Mario Galaxy (2026), and Obsession (2025). Best Buy is also selling some older titles on Blu-ray, including It’s a Wonderful Life (1943), Saving Private Ryan (1998), and The Godfather (1972). Most of the Blu-rays are available for purchase online and can be delivered to an address or picked up at a Best Buy store within a few days. As of this writing, The Odyssey appears to be in stock at Best Buy stores, as it’s currently listed as available for pickup within as little as an hour. Read full article Comments

title: Muse privacy invasions are freaking out Meta staffers, internal chats show
abstract: After some early adopters of Meta’s Muse AI agent complained that it was spying on private messages and behaving unpredictably earlier this fall, Reuters exposed internal chats showing that Meta staff had raised the same alarms. When testing the agent, staff warned that Muse appeared to be accessing encrypted private messages that users did not expect the bot to review, could be mixing up conversations between users, and even potentially sharing sensitive information users would never expect to be exposed. Some unexpected Muse outputs responded to questions that staffers never asked. Read full article Comments

title: Trump admin orders Kalshi to halt wagers on what words Trump will say
abstract: The Trump administration ordered prediction market Kalshi to stop offering event contracts that pay out based on whether President Trump will say a specific word before a particular date. Kalshi halted trading in the contracts while the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) conducts a review into whether the Trump mention contracts violate federal law. CNBC reported yesterday that "Kalshi quietly paused trading in a handful of 'mention' contracts tied to President Donald Trump at the end of last week at the request of the CFTC." Kalshi told media outlets that it is complying with the CFTC order. The markets taken down by Kalshi allowed users to wager on whether Trump would say certain words, including nicknames and the names of countries and companies. A similar expired event contract that can still be viewed on Kalshi's website asked whether Trump would use the nicknames "Marjorie Traitor Greene," "Sleepy Joe," and "Whack Job" or "Wack Job" before April 2026. title: The "shameful" measles data that lost the US its elimination status
abstract: International health authorities formally announced on Tuesday that the US has lost its measles elimination status, a hard-fought public health triumph won in 2000 after decades-long vaccination efforts. The loss had been widely expected by public health experts for months, and the decision was leaked by the press last week. Still, having the designation officially stripped stings. After the announcement Tuesday, public health experts, doctors, and political leaders decried the dramatic backslide for the US, calling it " shameful " and a " national embarrassment ." News articles point to the staggering vertical rise of measles cases this year, currently over 5,400 cases , more than any other year since 1991. An explosive measles outbreak in Pennsylvania accounts for over 1,500 of those cases . There have been 10 confirmed deaths across three states, several deaths just in the last week. But the measles data that caused the US to lose its status—the bits of it that are public at least—paint a darker picture of where the US is in its rematch with measles, the most contagious virus known on Earth. For one thing, almost none of the data from this year—the cases, the explosive Pennsylvania outbreak, the deaths—factored in to the loss. It was lost earlier. What's happening now is a runaway epidemic. Read full article Comments

title: Will Wright's next simulation will use AI to mine content from your memories
abstract: The computer gaming world hasn't heard much from Will Wright ( SimCity , The Sims ) since the underwhelming release of Spore in 2008 and Wright's subsequent departure from Maxis owner EA . Now, well over 15 years later, Wright is starting to promote his next digital simulation, which will use generative AI technology to craft a game-like experience from players' memories. MyMems , which is slated to release next year, differentiates itself from Wright's previous projects by "turn[ing] the simulation inward," as Wright's Gallium Studios and partner Artificial Agency put it in a press release this morning . The game will mine memories provided by the player to create digital people that can then form teams to solve puzzles in the game world. “If my Grandmother ended up in a Grand Slam match against Serena Williams, who would win?" Wright says by way of example in the release. "If I had to build a bridge across a short chasm, which three people from my life would I choose to help me?" Read full article Comments

title: What’s With All These Outages?
abstract: This week on “Uncanny Valley,” we discuss the outages that have swept digital life over the past week, where new money from Anthropic’s IPO is going, and the AI chip world post-Jensen Huang.

title: The Jensen Huang Blast Radius Has Hit His Favorite Restaurants
abstract: In Taiwan, some food vendors are distancing themselves from Nvidia’s former CEO. Others stand by him. “It’s not as if he killed someone or set something on fire,” says one shop owner.

title: Google Built a Giant ‘Mirror Dimension’ Internet to Test Its Chrome AI Agents
abstract: The company’s alternate-universe internet serves as a massive sandbox that allows the Chrome team to properly train AI browsing agents—without the risk of them going rogue.

title: Anthropic’s Record-Breaking IPO Highlights the AI Giant’s Worst Enemy—Itself
abstract: Investors betting a barnstorming $107 billion will weigh whether the company’s AI safety strategy and growing public anger toward data centers could impact its growth.

title: Does Nvidia Got This? Interim CEO Colette Kress Says It’s Got This
abstract: WIRED is tallying up how many times Nvidia’s interim CEO has assured everyone that the company has everything under control.

title: Even His Own Officials Don’t Think Trump’s China Trip Will Lead to Progress on AI
abstract: Fallout from the Nvidia scandal has made any negotiations around AI difficult, officials say.

abstract: The Trump administration announced plans to clamp down on China’s access to AI chips. Apparently, the cheating scandal of the century was the motivation they were missing.

title: Inside Nvidia’s First Post-Jensen All-Hands: Pay Raises and More Equity

title: Artex Is Criminals’ New Favorite ‘Point-and-Shoot’ AI Hacking Tool
abstract: Artex and similar penetration testing tools allow newbie hackers to scan targeted systems for vulnerabilities and successfully wage attacks using prompts fed to chatbots.

title: ‘Just Ridiculous’: A Famed Philosopher Takes on AI Consciousness
abstract: Thomas Nagel has done landmark work on consciousness in nonhumans; this week, he won the million-dollar Berggruen Prize for his contributions to the field. And he has a lot of thoughts on AI.

title: 같은 GPU로 더 많은 AI 요청을 처리할 수 있을까? ― KV 캐시 오프로딩 × EPP 라우팅: 계산 결과를 오래 남기고, 다음 요청이 그 결과를 찾아가게 하기

title: 지표 뒤에 숨은 맥락을 한눈에: New20 Timeline Hub 만들기
abstract: 대시보드에서 지표가 갑자기 움직인 날을 발견하면, 분석가는 자연스럽게 이유를 찾기 시작합니다. 그런데 숫자를 파고들기 전에 먼저 답해야 하는 질문이 있어요. “그날 제품에서 무슨 일이 있었을까요?” 새로운 화면이 배포됐을 수도 있고, 대상 유저 조건이 바뀌었을 수도 있습니다. 실험이 시작됐거나 혜택 정책이 달라졌을 수도 있죠. 이 기록들은 대개 어딘가에 남아 있지만, 한곳에 모여 있지는 않습니다. 배포 채널을 검색하고, 관련 PR을 찾아보고, 정책 문서와 논의 이력을 비교해야 비로소 당시의 상황을 그릴 수 있어요. 이 글에서는 페이스페이 프로모션 New20의 맥락을 한눈에 살펴보기 위해 만든 New20 Timeline Hub 를 소개합니다. 흩어진 기록을 어떻게 하나의 시간축으로 연결했는지, 자동으로 모은 정보를 어떤 기준으로 정리했는지, 그리고 신뢰할 수 있는 맥락을 만들기 위해 무엇을 고민했는지 이야기해 보겠습니다. 질문은 반복되는데, 답은 흩어져 있었습니다 New20은 참여한 유저가 일정 기간 페이스페이로 결제할 때 혜택을 제공하는 프로모션입니다. 반복 결제를 유도하는 것이 목표인 만큼, 혜택 정책뿐 아니라 참여 대상, 유저가 만나는 화면, 노출 지면, 실험이 계속 바뀝니다. 이런 제품을 분석하다 보면 비슷한 질문을 자주 받습니다. “9월 둘째 주에 참여가 왜 튀었나요?” ”지금 NAU 대상 조건이 정확히 어떤건가요?” ”이 경로로 들어오면 어떤 화면이 뜨나요?” ”그 때 쿠폰은 얼마였죠?” 답을 찾는 데 필요한 자료는 회의록 , GitHub PR, 정책 문서, 디자인 보드, 세그먼트 정의, 대시보드에 나뉘어 있었습니다. 관련 자료가 없어서가 아니라 기록을 이어 붙이는 비용 이 문제였어요. 각 자료는 자기 목적에는 충실했지만, 분석가가 특정 시점의 제품 상태를 복원하기에는 조각이 흩어져 있었습니다. 예를 들어 지표가 오른 시점에 배포가 있었다는 사실만 알아서는 충분하지 않습니다. 어떤 유저를 대상으로 했는지, 어떤 화면에서 노출됐는지, 같은 기간 다른 실험은 없었는지도 함께 살펴봐야 합니다. 게다가 변경 시점이 가깝다는 사실만으로 지표 변화의 원인을 확정할 수는 없습니다. 맥락은 인과관계의 답이라기보다, 어떤 가설을 검증해야 할지 찾는 출발점 에 가깝습니다. 힌트는 하나의 시간축에 있었습니다 허브를 만들 때 참고한 것은 Meta의 Timeline 형식 내부 도구 를 커머스 도메인의 배포 조회 도구에 적용한 사례였습니다. 커머스 사례에서는 팀과 서비스별로 한 줄씩 두고, 배포를 점으로 표시한 뒤 변경 유형을 색으로 구분했어요. 여러 변경을 같은 시간축에서 볼 수 있다는 점이 인상적이었습니다. 저는 이 방식을 분석가의 질문에 맞게 가져왔습니다. 배포만 나열하는 대신 제품 맥락을 다섯 가지 갈래로 나눴어요. 정책·혜택: 어떤 혜택과 운영 정책이 바뀌었는지 세그먼트: 누구에게 적용되는지, 대상 조건이 어떻게 달라졌는지 노출 지면: 유저가 어디에서 어떤 화면과 메시지를 만나는지 실험: 무엇을 검증하기 위해 어떤 시도를 했는지 데이터·대시보드: 분석과 모니터링에 필요한 데이터가 어떻게 연결되는지 이렇게 나누면 날짜는 하나로 유지하면서도 질문에 따라 필요한 갈래를 살펴볼 수 있습니다. 예를 들어 참여 지표를 이해하려면 정책 변경뿐 아니라 같은 시기의 노출 지면과 실험도 함께 확인할 수 있어요. 타임라인의 점에는 상태도 표시했습니다. 채운 점은 PR이나 배포를 통해 개발 반영이 확인된 변경 , 빈 점은 논의 기록은 있지만 개발 반영이 확인되지 않은 항목 입니다. 논의된 내용과 실제 반영된 내용을 같은 확실성으로 읽지 않도록 하기 위해서예요. 여러 기록을 하나의 ‘변경’으로 묶기 타임라인을 만들 때 부딪힌 문제는 관련 링크를 날짜순으로 늘어놓는 것만으로는 제품의 변화를 이해하기 어렵다는 점이었습니다. 하나의 제품 변경이 서버와 프론트엔드 PR, 데이터 작업, 배포 요약, 운영 논의 등의 여러 채널에 각각 기록되기 때문입니다. 예를 들어 9월 8일로 정리된 ‘현장참여 사후적립 출시’ 항목에는 PR 9건과 회의록 5건, 총 14개의 근거가 연결돼 있습니다. 이 변경에는 매장에서 먼저 결제한 유저가 이후 New20에 참여했을 때 적립을 사후에 지급하는 내용과 함께 안내·알림 퍼널, 인앱 진입점 관련 변경, 미수령 세그먼트 뷰가 연결돼 있었어요. 일부 서버·프론트엔드 반영과 관련 후속 작업은 서로 다른 날짜에 걸쳐 있었습니다. 이 기록들을 각각 별도의 점으로만 보여주면 실제로는 하나의 흐름인 일이 여러 사건처럼 보일 수 있습니다. 반대로 하나로 묶기만 하고 원문을 남기지 않으면, 요약이 무엇을 근거로 하는지 확인하기 어렵습니다. 그래서 허브에서는 변경을 읽기 쉬운 단위로 묶되, 그 판단에 사용한 원문을 함께 연결 했습니다. 이 방식의 핵심은 요약을 정답으로 만드는 데 있지 않습니다. 필요한 사람이 변경의 개요를 빠르게 파악하고, 중요한 판단을 할 때는 원문으로 돌아가 확인할 수 있게 하는 데 있습니다. 시간순 목록을 넘어, 질문별로 찾아보기 같은 자료라도 질문에 따라 필요한 출발점은 다릅니다. 그래서 허브에는 시간축 외에도 제품 맥락을 다른 관점에서 볼 수 있는 화면을 두었습니다. 히스토리: 날짜별 변경과 연결된 근거를 확인합니다. 노출 현황: 진입 경로와 유저 상태에 따라 어떤 화면이 보이는지 살펴봅니다. 세그먼트: 현재 대상 조건과 과거 변경 이력을 함께 봅니다. 관계 보기: 같은 주제에 속한 결정, 화면, 문서를 연결해서 탐색합니다. 쿠폰 발급 종료: 지면별 종료 현황을 확인합니다. 데이터: 대시보드, 리포트, 정책 문서로 이동합니다. 출처·범위: 어떤 자료를 모았고 어디에 빈틈이 있는지 확인합니다. 예전에는 “현재 대상 조건이 뭐죠?”라는 질문에 답하려면 SQL과 문서, 변경 스레드를 각각 찾아 맞춰 봐야 했습니다. 허브에서는 세그먼트 화면에서 현재 조건과 변경 이력을 함께 살펴볼 수 있습니다. “그날 무슨 일이 있었죠?”라는 질문은 히스토리에서 날짜를 좁힌 뒤 관련 원문으로 이동하는 방식으로 풀 수 있고요. 중요한 것은 모든 정보를 한 화면에 복사하는 것이 아니라, 질문에서 근거까지 이어지는 경로를 짧게 만드는 것 이었습니다. 매일 쌓이는 맥락을 정리하는 방법 허브가 한 번 만든 뒤 멈춘 문서가 되지 않도록, 매일 아침 기록을 수집하고 정리하는 과정을 붙였습니다. 1. 기록이 있는 곳에서 모읍니다 배포 요약 채널, 여러 저장소의 PR, 문서 목록, 결정 노트 등 자동으로 가져올 수 있는 자료부터 모았습니다. PR은 서버가 매시간 별도로 가져오고, 다른 자료는 아침 스크립트로 정리합니다. 아침 스크립트 실행에는 약 5~10분이 걸립니다. 모든 소스를 한꺼번에 완벽하게 연결하기보다, 먼저 기존에 기록이 쌓이고 있는 곳을 파악하는 것이 출발점이었어요. 2. 기록된 날짜와 실제 맥락의 날짜를 구분합니다 자동 수집에서 가장 어려운 문제 중 하나는 날짜였습니다. 어떤 결정이 나중에 지식 노트에 적재되면, 적재일을 사건의 날짜로 착각하기 쉽습니다. 하지만 분석가에게 필요한 것은 대개 노트가 저장된 날이 아니라, 결정이나 변경이 실제로 일어난 시점 입니다. 예를 들어 5월 15일에 논의한 내용이 9월 30일에 지식 노트로 적재된 경우가 있었습니다. 허브에서는 노트의 적재일을 그대로 쓰지 않고 근거가 되는 논의 시점을 확인해 날짜를 바로잡았습니다. 그렇지 않았다면 수개월이 지난 뒤의 지표 변화와 과거 논의가 잘못 나란히 놓일 수 있었겠죠. 3. 갈래와 상태를 붙이고, 표현을 정리합니다 수집한 항목은 정책·혜택, 세그먼트, 노출 지면, 실험, 데이터·대시보드 중 적절한 갈래로 나눕니다. 개발 반영이 확인됐는지, 논의만 확인됐는지도 구분합니다. 읽는 사람을 위해 표현도 정리했습니다. 이름을 가리고, 내부에서 쓰는 ‘편입’ 같은 단어는 맥락에 맞게 ‘참여’로 통일했어요. 기록을 모으는 일과 다른 사람이 이해할 수 있도록 맥락을 번역하는 일은 별개의 작업이었습니다. 4. 요약 옆에 원문을 남깁니다 각 항목에는 확인 가능한 PR, 회의록, 지식 노트 링크를 연결했습니다. 자동으로 만든 요약이나 수작업으로 정리한 문장 모두 틀릴 수 있기 때문입니다. 특히 정

title: 판단에만 집중하세요: 토스 타겟팅 모델 개발 자동화
abstract: 불과 2년 전만 해도 모델을 하나 만들려면 내부망에서 Jupyter 노트북을 켜고, 쿼리를 짜고, 수많은 함수를 직접 만들어야 했어요. 그런데 저희는 ML Engineer(MLE)가 반복적이고 번거로운 일보다는, 현재 일의 성과를 더 개선하기 위한 점을 찾고 임팩트를 줄 일에 집중하는데 더 많은 시간을 써야 한다고 생각했습니다. 그래서 고객 타겟팅 모델 개발 프레임워크 TASTE 를 꾸준히 가다듬어 모델 학습 시간을 2주에서 1일로 줄였어요. 그러나 모델 사용처로부터 받는, 그리고 모델을 개발한 MLE 스스로 묻는 "이 모델을 써도 되나?"라는 질문에 답하기 위한 판단 과정에서 늘 필요한 모델 비교와 평가 및 모니터링은 여전히 손으로 해야 했어요. 저희는 그 과정을 TASTE의 파이프라인에 더했어요. 이 글에서는 MLE 가 모델 하나를 쓰기까지 거치는 비교 네 가지를 차례로 따라가며, 각각을 어떻게 자동화했는지 소개합니다. 모델 하나를 쓰기까지 네 번 비교해요 TASTE 에서는 설정 파일 하나로 후보 피쳐 수집 → 피쳐 선정 → 학습 → 추론·적재 → 평가가 하나의 파이프라인으로 돌아요. 그런데 이 파이프라인이 내놓은 모델을 쓸지 판단하기 위해 다음 네 가지 질문에 답해야 했고, 이를 위한 계산을 사람이 따로 해야 했습니다. 질문 무엇과 무엇을 비교하나 예전 지금 1️⃣ 피쳐를 몇 개 쓸까 피쳐 수 K 끼리 MLE 가 경험으로 비율을 정함 auto_k 가 K 별 성능을 재서 고름 2️⃣ 어떤 구조를 쓸까 트리와 딥러닝 단계별 트리 여러 개를 곱한 조합을 손으로 비교 같은 평가셋으로 나란히 재서 고름 3️⃣ 기존 모델보다 나은가 새 모델과 기존 모델 점수와 정답을 손으로 조인 학습이 끝나면 평가 보고서가 나옴 4️⃣ 입력 데이터를 믿어도 되나 날짜끼리 (학습 때와 오늘, 평가일 사이) 확인하지 않음 결손이 한도를 넘으면 적재를 멈추고, 평가는 여러 날짜에서 함 1️⃣ 피쳐를 몇 개 쓸까: auto_k 피쳐 선택 이후 남은 고민 모델 성능을 기준으로 사용할 피쳐 수를 자동으로 고르는 auto_k 알고리즘은 팀 채팅 스레드에서 시작했어요. 지금까지 피쳐 수는 MLE가 정한 비율로 정했어요. 후보 피쳐를 중요도 순으로 세운 뒤 상위 몇 %만 남기는 방식이에요. 이 방식은 데이터 개수나 예측 대상의 특성과 상관없이 같은 비율을 쓰기 때문에 학습 효율과 성능이 떨어질 수 있습니다. 도메인·데이터·모델마다 알맞은 비율이 달라, MLE가 경험만으로 ‘상위 몇 %’를 자신 있게 정하기도 어렵죠. 먼저 대안으로 떠올린 건 중요도가 급격히 떨어지는 지점(Elbow)에서 자르는 방법이었어요. 그러나 이 방법으로 피쳐 갯수를 자른 다음(ex. 20개) 모형 성능을 평가하면, 이보다 더 많은 피쳐 수(ex. 75개)를 포함한 모형의 성능 지표가 훨씬 높은 경우가 많이 발생했어요. 이는 중요도가 몇 개 피쳐에 크게 몰려 있어 중요도가 급히 떨어지는 점이 구조적으로 앞쪽에서 포착되는데, 그 점에서 자르고 나도 여전히 모형 성능 개선에 기여하는 피쳐는 남아있기 때문이었습니다. 피쳐 수 (K) AUROC PR-AUC 458개와 PR-AUC 차이 상위 5% 회수율 20 99.1% 77.4% 유의하게 낮음 91.5% 30 99.5% 74.2% 유의하게 낮음 93.5% 50 100.0% 88.7% 유의하게 낮음 99.4% 75 100.1% 98.4% 구별 안 됨 100.8% 100 100.2% 100.0% 구별 안 됨 101.2% 458 100% 100% 기준 100% 결국 중요도 곡선의 모양만 보고 사용 피쳐 수의 컷오프 점을 정하는 방식은 적절하지 않았던 것입니다. 필요한 건 ‘성능이 어디서 더 오르지 않는가’였고, 그건 성능을 직접 재야 알 수 있었어요. 그래서 검증에 쓴 절차를 그대로 자동화한 것이 auto_k 예요(자체 조어). 요약하면, 같은 모델 설정에서 피쳐 수를 늘려가며 성능을 측정하고, 성능 개선이 멈추는 지점에서 사용할 최적의 피쳐 수를 결정해 보자는 아이디어예요. 이 방법을 검증하기 위해 어떤 모델의 후보로 걸러진 피쳐 458개를 피쳐 중요도(Feature Importance) 순으로 줄여 가며 성능을 쟀어요. 위 표에서 458개와 통계적으로 구별되지 않는 가장 작은 개수는 75개였어요. 피쳐를 84% 줄여도 유의한 성능 손실이 없으면서, 모델의 훈련시간이나 메모리는 절감할 수 있었죠. 그래서 중요도로 순서를 정하고, 성능으로 개수를 정했어요. auto_k는 이렇게 동작해요 auto_k는 위 실험을 그대로 자동화한 기능입니다. 후보 피쳐 전체로 트리를 한 번 학습해 피쳐 중요도 순위를 매겨요. 샘플 데이터에 대해서, 사용할 피쳐의 수 K = 10, 20, 30, 50, 75, 100, 150 등 마다 상위 K개로 다시 학습하고, 가장 최근 기간의 평가셋에서 PR-AUC를 재요. 최고점과 통계적으로 구별되지 않는 K 중 가장 작은 값을 골라요. 앞 표에서는 75예요. 어떤 K 도 최고점과 구별되지 않으면 판단할 근거가 없다고 보고, 기존 비율 방식을 그대로 써요. 피쳐를 줄이고도 성능은 높아졌어요. 한 상품의 구매 전환을 고객별로 예측하는 모델은 모델 구조를 딥러닝에서 트리로 바꾸고 (실험 내용은 2️⃣절의 딥러닝 vs Tree 참조), auto_k로 피쳐를 고르자, 피쳐를 절반 넘게 줄이면서도 상위 5% 회수율이 고관여 세그먼트 대비 약 1.7배 올랐습니다. 또한 실제 마케팅 메시지 발송 실험에서도 성과가 이어졌어요. auto_k로 피쳐를 고른 또 다른 상품 모델의 점수 상위 1% 고객은 기존 규칙 기반 세그먼트보다 클릭률이 약 5배, 신청 전환율이 약 2.6배 높았어요. 연령 구성을 맞춰 비교해도 클릭률은 3배 이상, 신청 전환율은 2배 이상 높았어요. 2️⃣ 어떤 구조를 쓸까: 트리와 딥러닝을 나란히 재요 모델 구조를 고를 때도 같은 데이터·같은 평가셋에서 성능을 비교해요. 노출 → 진입 → 클릭 → 신청처럼 단계가 이어지는 퍼널 모델은 종래에는 단계마다 트리 모델을 따로 학습해 왔어요. 진입할 확률, 진입한 고객이 상품을 누를 확률, 누른 고객이 신청할 확률을 각각 학습한 뒤 추론이 끝나면 점수를 곱해 최종 점수를 만들었습니다. 운영도 해석도 쉬운 방식이지만 단계끼리 서로 남남이라는 한계가 있었습니다. 진입 단계 모델이 배운 신호가 클릭·신청 모델로 전달되지 않아요. 데이터가 가장 적은 마지막 단계(신청)일수록 앞 단계에서 쌓인 신호가 절실한데 그걸 쓰지 못했죠. 조합을 고르는 일에도 손이 많이 갔어요. 3단계 퍼널 하나에 모델을 최대 다섯 개 학습하고 점수를 곱하는 조합 열한 가지의 성능을 직접 비교했습니다. 채널(푸시·홈 화면·메시지)이 바뀌면 이 과정을 통째로 다시 했고, 퍼널이 수십 개다 보니 운영하는 트리 모델도 수십 개로 불어났어요. 그래서 지금은, 퍼널 전체를 한 모델로 학습하는 딥러닝 모델 AITM(Adaptive Information Transfer Multi-task, KDD 2021)을 TASTE 설정에서 고를 수 있게 구현했습니다. 이 모델이 우리의 최선이라고 믿는 것은 아니지만 앞으로도 확장성 높고 유연한 프레임워크 덕분에 다양한 모델의 형상을 추가할 수 있어요. 퍼널 모델 구조와 라벨 설계 퍼널 모델인 AITM 이 ‘추론한 뒤에 곱하기’와 갈라지는 지점은 두 장치입니다. 정보 전달 (Adaptive Information Transfer): 앞 단계에서 학습한 표현에 변환을 적용한 뒤, 현재 단계의 표현과 Attention 으로 결합해요. 앞 단계 정보를 얼마나 참고할지 고객마다 가중치로 정하는 셈이에요. 단조성 제약 (Label Constraint): 뒤 단계 확률이 앞 단계 확률보다 커지면 그 초과분만큼 손실에 벌점을 더해요. 아래 그림은 단계별 표현이 정보 전달 모듈을 거쳐 다음 단계로 넘어가는 AITM 의 구조예요. 이 모델을 쓰려고 파이프라인을 새로 짜지는 않습니다. TASTE 설정에서 퍼널 모델을 고르고, 단계별 정답을 한 테이블에 나란히 담아 주면 돼요. 퍼널 라벨 테이블 컬럼 운영에 쓰는 점수 2단계 사용자 ID, 기준일, label_a, label_b 마지막 단계(B) 점수 3단계 사용자 ID,

title: Closing the GitHub Actions Monitoring Gap: Observing ARC Runners with an Exporter
abstract: Hi, I’m Uno from the Delivery part of Karrot’s SRE team. Our team’s mission is to run Kontrol, our internal deployment platform on Kubernetes, and manage the company-wide CI system that mostly relies on GitHub Actions. In this post I’ll introduce the exporter we built to see which Jobs are waiting and which Runner is running each Job. I’ll also share how we improved it in production. A Workflow defines what happens when an event such as a push or pull request occurs. Each Workflow is split into Jobs such as test and build that run on execution environments called Runners. If no Runner is free, a Job waits until one becomes available. name: Simple # 1. Workflow: defines the automation on: workflow_dispatch: jobs: run_shell_command: # 2. Job: the unit that gets a Runner and runs name: Actions are amazing runs-on: arc-test-runner steps: # 3. Step: the commands the Job executes - name: Say hello run: | echo "Hello!" Runners can be GitHub-hosted or self-hosted. At Karrot we mainly use self-hosted Runners on our own Kubernetes clusters. These are managed by a Kubernetes operator called ARC (Actions Runner Controller) . ARC organizes Runners into groups called Runner Scale Sets and scales each set according to Job demand. Each set defines the Runner image and resources, along with minimum and maximum Runner counts. A Workflow can specify a Runner Scale Set in runs-on so its Jobs are assigned to Runners in that set. Source: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/runners/actions-runner-controller Even with autoscaling, Jobs don’t always start immediately. A GitHub outage or a spike in Job requests can leave them stuck in the Queued state. While operating ARC, we often heard developers say, “My Action is stuck in Queued and won’t run.” Answering that question wasn’t easy with the data we had. We often had to wait for an announcement on GitHub’s status page or infer the cause from ARC’s built-in metrics. ARC’s built-in metrics show aggregate counts of Runners and Jobs, but they don’t tell us how many Jobs are waiting for a Runner, how long they’ve been waiting, or which Runner Pod is running a given Job. With that information, we could give developers a better understanding of what was happening with their Jobs. While looking for a solution, we found an issue in the ARC repository proposing to add Job information to Runner Pods as labels. Adopting that approach would require controller changes and additional permissions, as well as a separate setup to collect the labels as metrics, so we decided to build our own solution. We built action-runner-job-exporter to connect Runner Pods to their Assigned Jobs and track Jobs still waiting for a Runner. There are three key components for the exporter, which are separate binaries. Collector associates Job names with Runner Pods, Webhook tracks waiting Jobs, and StateStore persists Webhook's state. action-runner-job-exporter architecture How ARC Runners work Before getting into the exporter, let’s look at how ARC creates a Runner Pod and how a Job reaches it. Each Runner Scale Set has a Listener Pod that keeps a session open with GitHub and waits for new Job assignments. A Workflow starts in a repository, and GitHub assigns each Job to the Runner Scale Set that matches its runs-on. The Listener works out how many Runners are needed from the assigned Jobs and the min/max Runner settings, then updates the replicas of the EphemeralRunnerSet. ARC creates that many EphemeralRunner resources, fetches a one-time registration config (JIT config) from GitHub for each, and starts the Runner Pods. Once a Runner Pod registers with GitHub, GitHub assigns a Job to it. After the Job starts, the Listener receives the assignment and writes the repository and Job details into the status field of that EphemeralRunner. The Runner process exits after the Job finishes and ARC cleans up the Runner’s resources. Runner creation and Job assignment ARC creates the Runners and GitHub decides which Job goes to each one. B

title: GitHub Actions 모니터링의 빈칸: Exporter로 ARC Runner 관측하기
abstract: 안녕하세요, 당근 SRE팀 딜리버리 파트에서 일하고 있는 Uno(우노)예요. 딜리버리 파트는 Kubernetes 환경 기반의 사내 배포 플랫폼 Kontrol을 운영하고 GitHub Actions 중심의 전사 CI 시스템을 관리해요. 이번 글에서는 GitHub Actions를 운영하며 Job의 대기 현황과 Job을 실행 중인 Runner를 파악하기 위해 exporter를 만들고 개선한 과정을 소개할게요. exporter를 소개하기에 앞서 GitHub Actions의 구조를 간단히 살펴볼게요. GitHub Actions에서는 push나 Pull Request 같은 이벤트가 발생했을 때 실행할 작업의 흐름을 Workflow로 정의해요. 하나의 Workflow는 테스트, 빌드처럼 여러 Job으로 나뉘어 각 Job은 Runner라는 실행 환경에 배정되어 실행되고 할당 가능한 Runner가 없으면 Job은 배정될 때까지 대기해요. name: Simple # 1. Workflow: 자동화 작업 정의 on: workflow_dispatch: jobs: run_shell_command: # 2. Job: Runner 배정 및 실행 단위 name: Actions are amazing runs-on: arc-test-runner steps: # 3. Step: 작업 실행 절차 및 명령 - name: Say hello run: | echo "Hello!" GitHub Actions의 Job을 실행하는 Runner는 크게 GitHub이 관리하는 GitHub-hosted Runner와 GitHub 외부에서 운영하는 self-hosted Runner 두 가지로 나뉘어요. 당근은 Kubernetes 환경에서 직접 운영하는 self-hosted Runner를 주로 사용하고 이 Runner는 ARC(Actions Runner Controller) 라는 Kubernetes 오퍼레이터로 관리해요. ARC는 Runner Scale Set 단위로 Runner를 관리하고 대기 중인 Job 수에 맞춰 Runner 수를 조절해요. Runner Scale Set에는 Runner의 이미지와 리소스 및 최소, 최대 수를 설정할 수 있고 Workflow의 runs-on에 Runner Scale Set을 지정하면 해당 Runner에 Job이 배정돼요. 출처: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/runners/actions-runner-controller Runner 수가 자동으로 조절되지만 모든 Job이 즉시 실행되지는 않고 GitHub 장애가 발생하거나 Job 요청이 급증해 실행이 지연되면 Queued 상태로 표시돼요. ARC로 Runner를 운영하면서 가장 자주 받은 문의도 “GitHub Action이 Queued 상태로 실행되지 않아요.”였어요. 하지만 상황 파악을 위한 데이터가 부족해서 GitHub 상태 페이지에 공지가 올라오기를 기다리거나 ARC가 기본적으로 제공하는 메트릭으로 원인을 추측할 수밖에 없었어요. ARC 기본 메트릭으로 Runner와 Job의 집계 현황은 볼 수 있지만 Runner를 기다리는 Job 개수와 대기 시간, 어떤 Job이 어느 Runner Pod에서 실행되는지는 파악하기 어려웠어요. 이런 정보를 확인할 수 있다면 Job 실행을 기다리는 개발자분들께 현재 상황을 더 명확하게 안내할 수 있을 거라고 생각했고 해결책을 찾던 중 Runner Pod에 Job 정보를 라벨로 추가하자는 ARC 이슈 를 발견했어요. 하지만 이 방식은 컨트롤러 변경과 권한 추가가 필요해 적용까지 시간이 걸릴 수 있었고 라벨을 메트릭으로 수집하는 구성도 따로 마련해야 해서 다른 방법을 찾아야 했어요. ⁠그래서 Runner Pod와 Job의 관계뿐만 아니라 대기 중인 Job까지 살펴볼 수 있도록 action-runner-job-exporter를 만들었어요. exporter는 Runner Pod에 Job 이름을 붙이는 Collector, Runner를 기다리는 Job을 추적하는 Webhook, Webhook의 상태를 저장하는 StateStore까지 세 개의 바이너리로 구성했어요. 지금부터 각 구성 요소를 만든 과정과 운영하며 개선한 내용을 소개할게요. action-runner-job-exporter 구조도 배경: ARC Runner가 생성되고 Job을 배정받기까지 Collector가 Runner와 Job을 어떻게 연결하는지 살펴보기 전에 ARC에서 Runner Pod가 생성되고 Job을 배정받는 과정을 먼저 알아볼게요. 각 Runner Scale Set의 Listener Pod는 GitHub과 세션을 맺고 새로운 Job 배정을 기다려요. 저장소에서 Workflow가 실행되면 GitHub은 각 Job의 runs-on에 맞는 Runner Scale Set에 Job을 배정해요. Listener는 배정된 Job과 최소·최대 Runner 설정을 바탕으로 필요한 Runner 수를 계산해서 EphemeralRunnerSet의 replicas를 변경해요. ARC가 필요한 수만큼 EphemeralRunner를 생성하고 GitHub에서 일회용 등록 설정(JIT config)을 받아와 Runner Pod를 띄워요. Runner Pod가 GitHub에 등록되면 GitHub은 해당 Runner에 Job을 배정해요. Job이 시작되면 Listener가 Job 배정 정보를 받아 해당 EphemeralRunner의 status 필드에 저장소와 Job 정보를 업데이트해요. Job이 끝나면 Runner 프로세스가 종료되고 ARC가 Runner 관련 리소스를 정리해요. Runner 생성, Job 배정 과정 ARC가 필요한 수만큼 Runner를 생성하면 각 Runner에 어떤 Job을 배정할지는 GitHub이 결정해요. Runner Pod는 특정 Job을 위해 생성되지 않으므로 Pod 이름만으로는 어떤 Job이 배정되었는지 알 수 없고 Listener가 EphemeralRunner의 status를 갱신해야 배정된 Job을 확인할 수 있어요. Collector: Runner Pod에 Job 이름 붙이기 exporter를 만든 목표는 개발자분들이 GitHub Actions의 상태를 문의하시기 전에 SRE가 GitHub Actions의 이상 징후를 먼저 파악하는 것이었어요. 그래서 가장 먼저 Runner Pod에서 어떤 Job을 실행하고 있는지 확인하고 싶었어요. Pod 라벨과 기존 메트릭에는 Job 정보가 없었지만 EphemeralRunner와 Runner Pod의 이름이 같다는 점을 이용하면 status에 기록된 Job 정보를 해당 Pod와 연결할 수 있다고 생각했어요. 이 아이디어로 Pod와 Job의 관계를 메트릭으로 확인할 수 있도록 첫 번째 바이너리인 Collector를 만들었어요. Collector는 Kubernetes informer로 EphemeralRunner의 생성, 변경, 삭제를 지켜보며 최신 상태를 메모리 캐시에 저장하고 이 캐시를 읽어 아래 메트릭을 제공해요. arc_runner_job_info{namespace, pod, runner_name, repository, job_name, workflow_ref, workflow_run_id} Collector는 Job이 시작되어 status.jobRepositoryName이 채워진 Runner에 대해서만 이 메트릭을 제공해요. workflow_run_id 라벨은 여러 Job을 이어서 작업을 정의하는 Workflow를 가리키는 값이라 https://github.com/<org>/<repo>/actions/runs/<workflow_run_id>로 실행 페이지 링크를 바로 만들 수 있게 구성했어요. Collector 구조도 Prometheus가 메트릭을 수집할 때 exporter Pod의 라벨과 이름이 겹쳐서 Runner Pod의 이름은 exported_pod에, Namespace는 exported_namespace에 담겨 있어요. 이 라벨을 컨테이너의 CPU, 메모리, 네트워크 사용량 메트릭(container_.*)에 있는 pod, namespace 라벨과 연결하면 사용량에 저장소와 Job 이름을 붙일 수 있어

title: Toward a Science of AI Agent Societies
abstract: AI agents are rapidly evolving from isolated personal assistants into networked actors that interact with one another at scale. We envision the emergence of AI agent societies, with their own social and economic dynamics, as a new research frontier. We argue that AI agent societies should be studied as a distinct object of inquiry: neither simply larger collections of individual agents nor merely simulations of human society. To formalize this perspective, we propose four core properties that a valid AI agent society should satisfy: individualized objectives, rules and governance, autonomy, and scale and complexity. Building on this framework, we identify four classes of societal behaviors worth studying in AI agent societies: economic behaviors, behaviors under conflict-of-interest, unsafe and unethical behaviors, and system-level behaviors. We then outline key technical challenges--including property parameterization, parameter balancing, and robust implementation--and argue that progress on these challenges could enable scientifically informative and practically useful models of AI agent societies. Finally, we revisit existing multi-agent systems through the lens of the proposed core properties, show that they instantiate only subsets of them, and discuss implications for platform design, evaluation, and governance.

title: Causal Discovery with False Positive Error Control
abstract: Causal discovery methods produce data-driven hypotheses about causal relationships, which may become new scientific findings or inform decisions about downstream interventions. In such settings, false positive causal claims can be more consequential than false negatives. Yet few methods target false positive error control in causal discovery, and existing error guarantees are often asymptotic and require strong versions of the faithfulness assumption. We introduce the $m$-conservative PC algorithm and prove that it controls false discovery rate in the linear Gaussian setting under an extremely weak version of the faithfulness assumption. In our framework, false positive error for causal graphs is defined based on the conditional-independence information they entail, yielding a metric that penalizes both false adjacencies and incorrect edge orientations. The parameter $m$ quantifies a trade-off between algorithmic complexity and the strength of the required faithfulness assumption. The $m$-conservative PC algorithm combines undirected graph learning, a Benjamini-Yekutieli-style procedure for conditional independence testing, and a conservative orientation step that marks unresolved or contradictory edge directions as ambiguous. Our algorithm produces valid outputs and retains error guarantees even in the finite-sample setting, despite possible random errors in the conditional independence tests.

title: Breaking Noise Shortcuts in Self-Supervised Learning Via Noise-Aligned View Generation
abstract: Self-supervised learning (SSL) is increasingly applied to scientific imaging domains, such as microscopy, where labels are scarce but noisy data is abundant. These domains exhibit significant signal-dependent noise, which can create a representational shortcut: since both augmented views derive from the same noisy image, the encoder can boost view agreement by also encoding noise patterns rather than semantic content. To enable noise-robust representation learning without knowledge of underlying noise models, we introduce Self-Aligned Noise Augmentation (SEANA), a drop-in module that generates noise-aware SSL views. SEANA learns an invertible variance-stabilizing transform (VST) from noisy data, then estimates the clean signal and resamples independent noise in learned VST space, requiring no clean targets, no dataset-specific denoiser training or use at inference, and no changes to the SSL objective or encoder. On CIFAR-10 and ImageNet-100 under synthetic Gaussian, Poisson-Gaussian, and multiplicative noise, SEANA improves clean-test linear-probe accuracy across contrastive/non-contrastive SSL methods, indicating higher-quality representations. On real fluorescence imaging, SEANA improves Jurkat cell-cycle stage classification by up to 28.6pp over standard SSL and 27.5pp over denoiser-preprocessed baselines. In all settings, SEANA outperforms the denoiser-preprocessed SSL pipelines, demonstrating that learned VST-space noise-aligned resampling yields more robust representations than denoising alone. Code is available at: https://github.com/opatil31/SEANA

title: φTD: Distributional Reinforcement Learning using Characteristic Functions
abstract: Distributional Reinforcement Learning methods aim to learn the entire distribution of returns, yet current algorithmic approaches are limited to a narrow class of distributions. We propose $\varphi$TD, a method to overcome this limitation by computing the loss in the frequency domain. We demonstrate that this further unifies quantile and categorical approaches to distributional RL, and enables the learning of distributions that were previously impossible to capture, such as mixtures of continuous distributions. We empirically study $\varphi$TD, across synthetic benchmarks and large-scale deep RL environments and demonstrate that the flexibility obtained from wider parametric families can lead to improved performance.

title: Decomposing SGD Dynamics in Neural Networks: Teacher-Induced Spikes and Variance Inflation
abstract: We study two-layer neural networks trained by stochastic gradient descent (SGD) on a multi-index teacher model, focusing on how first-layer parameters orthogonal to the teacher subspace affect generalization. We decompose the first-layer weights into a signal component aligned with the teacher and an orthogonal complement, and analyze their joint SGD dynamics together with the second layer in the proportional limit. We show that although SGD updates to the complement are initially isotropic, the training dynamics induce teacher-dependent spectral spikes in the complement Gram matrix. This emergent anisotropy provides a concrete mechanism by which representation variance is amplified, and generalization degrades. To isolate this effect, we introduce Decomposed Dynamics, an analytically tractable surrogate whose asymptotic test-error dynamics coincide with those of SGD. In simulations with a ReLU student, freezing the directions of the orthogonal complement improves generalization relative to training them. Finally, we show that the signal component rapidly aligns with the second-layer weights, revealing strong cross-layer coupling even in this shallow setting. Together, our results provide a dynamical explanation for how feature learning outside the teacher subspace harms generalization.

title: A Model of Diverse Sampling from Language Models
abstract: Language models often produce high-quality individual samples but poor sets, with repeated samples clustering around the same semantic modes. We formalize diverse generation as sampling a size-$K$ subset of complete strings from a determinantal point process (DPP), where the likelihood encodes item quality, and the embedding geometry encodes repulsion between similar outputs. Exact inference over all strings is intractable, so we propose PoolDPP: draw a finite candidate pool from a tractable proposal, importance-weight the candidates toward the target quality, and run a $K$-DPP sampler on the induced pool kernel; a greedy MAP variant provides deterministic selection. We prove a finite-sample bound with an explicit constant: the KL divergence between the sampler's output and the target $K$-DPP decays as O(1/N) in the pool size. Empirically, PoolDPP extends the quality--diversity frontier on open-ended generation and the precision--recall frontier on ambiguous text-to-SQL (Ambrosia), and on mathematical reasoning (GSM8K), it raises diversity at about the same pass@$K$.

title: Reconstruction vs. Prediction Pre-Training of Discrete Video Representations for Continuous Control
abstract: Self-supervised video encoders are commonly trained to either reconstruct pixels or predict latent features, yet it remains unclear how these objectives shape representations for downstream dynamics. We present a capacity-matched study isolating this choice: two identical video encoders with a shared FSQ bottleneck are trained under autoencoding and V-JEPA objectives on a continuous control environment. We introduce a simple asymmetric discretization scheme to apply the same bottleneck to the predictive model. The resulting representations exhibit a clear trade-off: the autoencoder preserves substantially more physical state information and achieves slightly better one-step latent prediction, while the predictive encoder accumulates less error under autoregressive rollout. Structural probes suggest that this advantage is associated with greater robustness to low-level visual perturbations and stronger dependence on temporal context. These results indicate that predictive and reconstructive objectives induce distinct representations of dynamics, trading state fidelity for properties that may benefit long-horizon prediction.

title: PsyWorld: Profile-Conditioned World Modeling for Human Behavior Prediction
abstract: Understanding how stable psychometric traits and time-varying states jointly inform behavior is an important problem in computational behavioral science. Existing personalized agents commonly condition actions directly on a static profile, leaving realized state transitions unused as an explicit source of supervision. We introduce a profile-conditioned state world model that uses observed environment--behavior state transitions to learn transition-informed representations for behavioral prediction. During training, a posterior encoder quantizes realized transitions, while a prior predicts the resulting codes from the psychometric profile and pre-transition context. The prior code and predicted next state then condition macro-level behavior and simulator-grounded execution. Thus, the world model provides structured transition supervision instead of treating personality as a direct action descriptor. We evaluate the framework in VEET, a controlled behavioral simulator with human trajectories, and in AgentSociety as a structurally different synthetic environment. A participant-disjoint split of 240 training, 25 validation, and 48 test participants evaluates generalization to unseen people. On VEET, the model reaches 0.904 Top-1 accuracy (95\% CI: [0.895, 0.913]) and 0.0033 Macro KL. Ablations associate continuous next-state modeling with most of the Top-1 gain, while discrete codes and prior alignment mainly improve Top-3 and distributional alignment. These results establish transition-informed world-model supervision as useful for subject-generalized behavior prediction, without implying causal psychological mechanisms or calibrated long-horizon state dynamics.

title: Choosing the Right Representations: Task-Aware Fusion for Multimodal Materials Language Models
abstract: Multimodal language models for materials science rely on effective mechanisms for incorporating three-dimensional structural representations. MatterChat addresses this challenge using a large bridge module between a pretrained structural encoder and the LLM, together with a separate contrastive alignment stage. We instead ask whether this bridge can adaptively select and combine representations from multiple structural encoders according to the target property. We find that supervised and generative material encoders provide complementary information for property prediction. We found that, for Zatom-1, this information is not concentrated in the final layer. Instead, the most informative representations occur at different depths depending on the target property. This motivates Task-Conditioned Attention Fusion (TCAF), a lightweight attention-based bridge that uses task-conditioned latent queries to combine CHGNet features with intermediate Zatom-1 representations. The bridge is trained directly on downstream prediction tasks, allowing representation selection and material-language alignment to be learned jointly without separate contrastive pretraining. Across classification and regression tasks, TCAF outperforms MatterChat, with up to 47.8% lower RMSE, while using substantially fewer trainable parameters and halving the overall training time. Further experiments incorporating UMA-S demonstrate TCAF's flexibility across encoder combinations, with the three-encoder configuration achieving the highest macro-average classification accuracy of 89.61%.

title: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Location Encoding Methods for Species Distribution Modelling
abstract: Understanding the spatial distribution of species is a key question in ecology. A variety of solutions, from statistical, traditional machine learning, through to deep learning-based methods have been proposed. These methods take sparse observations for a species of interest as input and aim to generate dense spatial outputs indicating the spatial range of the species. Orthogonal to the choice of statistical model used is the question of what input features are most informative. Thanks to recent developments, the number of options has greatly expanded, with choices spanning different climate variables, learning-based encodings, earth embedding models, or raw transformed geographic coordinates. In this work, we introduce a standardized evaluation framework and quantify the effectiveness of different location encodings in the context of species range estimation, both at the local and global scale.

title: ICICLE: In-Context Inference for Curve-Learning Extrapolation
abstract: Freeze-thaw Bayesian optimization allocates training budget by predicting how partially observed learning curves will continue. LC-PFN first applied prior-data fitted networks (PFNs) to learning-curve extrapolation, and FT-PFN extended this approach to configuration-aware freeze-thaw optimization with a ten-slot hyperparameter encoder. We introduce In-Context Inference for Curve-Learning Extrapolation (ICICLE), an in-context surrogate that accepts a variable number of hyperparameters through a shared set encoder and is trained on a synthetic prior covering typed hyperparameters, heavy-tailed noise, quantization, and divergence. ICICLE has 1.28 million parameters (8.7% of FT-PFN's count) and produces similar mean-regret trajectories to FT-PFN on LCBench, PD1, and TaskSet. On the 86-task Meta-Album benchmark with 33 hyperparameters, ICICLE reaches lower mean normalized regret than Quick-Tune overall and on extended, with no clear difference on mini or micro. It does so without pre-training or meta-training on Meta-Album tasks, whereas Quick-Tune is meta-trained on related Meta-Album tasks. Our release samples synthetic training tasks on the fly and provides a freeze-thaw scheduler for Ray Tune and an ONNX model for inference without JAX or PyTorch.

title: Harmonic Circuit: Chord Progression Lies in a Sparse Principal Information Flow in Symbolic Music Models
abstract: Mechanistic Interpretability (MI) seeks to decode neural network computations into human-understandable logic. A core methodology in MI is circuit discovery: identifying the information flow in sub-networks that drive specific model behaviors. While circuit discovery has matured within Natural Language Processing (NLP), the interpretable circuits in music models remain largely unexplored. In this work, we identify a music-functional circuit within two symbolic music generative models: ChatMusician and MuPT. The music function we consider is the prediction of the terminal tonic root in a classical harmonic progression pattern $I \ldots V \rightarrow I$. We use the Auto-Emergence algorithm to extract a principal sparse sub-network as the identified circuit. Validation via causal intervention confirms that this identified circuit is a primary driver of harmonic progression behaviors in the symbolic music models. To our knowledge, this represents the first systematic circuit-discovery study conducted within the music domain. Our demo page is available at: https://ukiyo23rui.github.io/auto-emergence-demo/.

title: MINT: Meeting-time Indicators for Truncation in Multi-Step Off-Policy RL
abstract: Many multi-step off-policy temporal-difference methods handle policy mismatch through products of per-step trace coefficients, leading to a trade-off between variance control and long-horizon signal. The maximum trace length consequently becomes a sensitive hyperparameter. We propose MINT (Meeting-time INdicators for Truncation), which replaces these products with a binary stopping indicator: one until coupled behavior and target trajectories first meet, zero thereafter. At the true value function, the indicator's idempotence yields a variance bound governed by meeting-time survival. For practical implementation, a single sampled action provides a model-free surrogate for the stopping rule, requiring no transition model or mixing-time estimate. We derive separate sufficient conditions for contraction of the state-coupled operator and its practical surrogate under fixed-policy evaluation. On MuJoCo and DeepMind Control tasks, MINT outperforms the reported multi-step baselines; the main MuJoCo comparison uses a common cap without per-task cap-length tuning. We also demonstrate the effectiveness of MINT on Atari 100k, RWRL, and OGBench experiments; MINT adapts the backup horizon to reduce target variability relative to long fixed-horizon backups across tasks and dynamics.

title: Rare-Tail Statistics For Learning Biased Gaussian Halfspaces with Label Noise
abstract: We revisit the classical problem of learning general Gaussian halfspaces in the presence of label noise, with particular focus on the large-bias regime, where information-computation gaps are conjectured in several standard label-noise models. Concretely, we present and analyze the rare-tail mean estimator, an extremely simple one-shot statistic that averages only the observed minority class. In the large-bias regime, classical Averaging (Servedio, 1999) and related global first-moment statistics are provably suboptimal, while the rare-tail mean estimator recovers the target halfspace direction at the information-theoretic sample rate (modulo log factors) under a broad class of label noise models, including probit noise and margin-dependent noise with very slow decay away from the boundary. Notably, our guarantees allow labels arbitrarily close to the decision boundary to be nearly random, while still giving strong directional recovery from a small number of samples. The estimator also cleanly interpolates between the noiseless and noisy regimes: without noise, it attains the same sample rate as classical separability-based methods for realizable halfspaces, and under low noise, or noise that decays away from the boundary, it keeps this rate even after linear separability has been destroyed. As an application, we consider a two-stage curriculum in which source samples, whose noise may be arbitrarily close to $1/2$ near the boundary and decay very slowly away from it, precede target samples, whose noise flips every label at the same rate, i.e., random classification noise (RCN). Since both stages share the same Bayes optimal halfspace, our estimator supplies the directional warm start needed by existing refinement routines, and together they learn the RCN target at the information-theoretic sample rate in the large-bias regime, up to log factors.

title: Fast Bayesian Methods for Uncertainty Quantification in Sparse AI Evaluation
abstract: Estimating how an AI system will perform on a new benchmark need not require another large model. We use public evaluation counts to choose a weak Beta prior, then update it exactly from at most 31 revealed outcomes. The predictor uses no item semantics, pretrained weights, or inference API. Its single online evaluation in the AIMS competition returned a team-reported Brier ALC of 0.188477, a 24.6% reduction from the constant-0.5 reference. The complete submission is 7,754 bytes; a server microbenchmark measures 12.71 microseconds per prediction with 31 matching labels. We describe how source evaluations are compressed into 301 prior means and show why a concentration of two lets new evidence rapidly determine the prediction. The resulting posterior gives exact uncertainty about the modelled success rate without numerical integration or neural inference. A public evaluation covers 79 system-benchmark pairs and eight seeds, reaching Brier ALC 0.200250 for the submitted method. Accompanying code and sufficient statistics reconstruct the fitted prior byte for byte and replay all 632 evaluation trajectories. The result demonstrates how much predictive value a compact Bayesian model can extract from sparse target feedback at very low online cost.

title: Rethinking Contrastive Targets in Radiology Language-Image Pretraining
abstract: CLIP-style contrastive image-text pretraining is widely used in radiology data, where each image is paired with one report and every other report in the batch is treated as a negative. Under this recipe, two failures appear, neither of which is systematically addressed by existing contrastive learning theory: zero-shot evaluation peaks then degrades while training loss keeps decreasing, and training fails to learn from large batches. We hypothesize the cause is structural rather than radiology-specific: many unpaired reports share clinical findings with a given image, so CLIP's paired-identity target is systematically biased, not merely noisy. To test this, we construct CLEVR-Radiology, a synthetic testbed that preserves only this overlapping-fact structure and reproduces both failures. With evidence that the structure is sufficient to reproduce the failures, we develop a target-misspecification theory that explains both failures from a single deterministic gradient bias amplified by batch size, and use it to motivate a minimal compatibility-based correction, CorLIP: text is treated as positive whenever its clinical assertions agree with the image, with no architecture changes. Beyond benchmark improvements, CorLIP largely removes the post-peak degradation, makes large-batch training succeed where it previously collapsed, substantially amplifies the gains from more data, and is the only configuration that remains stable up to B=2048. The correction transfers from chest X-ray to 3D CT modalities.

title: PGU-Decoder: Prior-Guided Unified Decoding for Industrial Road-Network Map Updating
abstract: Timely road-network map updates are essential to navigation and autonomous driving. Three key tasks are intra-intersection road network generation, merging/diverging detection, and drivable-area detection, covering topology, geometry, and attributes, respectively. Separate pipelines duplicate rule maintenance, quality assurance, and manual verification, increasing operational costs. We propose PGU-Decoder, a production-grade unified decoding framework for semantic prediction across these tasks. A Prior Query Module (PQM) constructs point-level prior queries from sampled locations on road-network geometries. Fixed reference points preserve positional priors throughout decoding, allowing the model to focus on surrounding context. Point-level representations are aggregated into instance-level representations, and a Relational Graph Attention Network (RGAT) captures inter-instance dependencies. Task-specific heads then generate predictions. We validate PGU-Decoder in large-scale automated road-network map updating across more than 360 cities in China, where it consistently outperforms seven baselines. Following deployment at AutoNavi Map, it achieves quality scores above 98% on all three tasks, reduces manual verification costs by 95%, and increases update frequency from weekly to hourly. These results demonstrate a practical and cost-effective industrial solution for road-network map updating.

title: MLE Agents: Autonomous ML Engineering in Large-scale Recommendation Systems
abstract: The typical workflow for improving large-scale ranking and recommendation models is slow and tedious: an engineer forms a hypothesis, implements it as a code change, trains a model, and evaluates it both offline and online, often relying on their own intuition and experience along the way. Autonomous LLM agents promise to speed this up by running the loop on their own, but it is still unclear whether they can do this in industry-scale systems rather than on benchmarks or small proxy tasks. We build human-on-the-loop machine learning engineer (MLE) agents that propose, implement, train, and evaluate model changes on large-scale search rankers. Engineers retain control over objective design, search direction, and final-model review. We identify three obstacles that make this industry setting challenging: feedback takes hours per experiment, offline metrics do not always predict online impact, and improvements saturate after the early wins. We address these with parallel training runs, an objective calibrated to match online impact, and careful context engineering. In one campaign, the system ran 1,097 completed candidate experiments and accepted 325, a 29.6\% acceptance rate compared with 15.6\% in the earlier campaign under a different objective and search constraint. Its best model increases search volume by 0.23\% in an A/B test of large scale. Several improvements were architectural changes the team had never tried, drawn from the broader industry and literature, suggesting that MLE agents can explore regions of the design space that human intuition overlooks. We find that the design of the harness around the model matters: intuition suggests that a stronger underlying model is enough, but in our experience, the design of the loop around it is just as critical. More broadly, our work shows that autonomous agents can do real machine-learning engineering in industry-scale systems.

title: A Rank-One Bypass of Fixed Linear Erasure
abstract: Linear concept erasure can make a target unreadable to a specified family of linear classifiers applied to a model's current internal features. In an open-weight release, however, an attacker can modify the layers that produce those features. We study a fixed affine erasure layer whose upstream model is allowed to change. If the layer transmits even one direction visible to an allowed downstream classifier, the attacker can write a target score into that direction and carry it through the layer. We show that this condition is also necessary, and that for a nonconstant linear target score the required change is a rank-one affine update. Across six CIFAR-10 class-pair tasks, the route restores nearly all pre-erasure target performance and can leave a deployed benign linear head's scores unchanged to numerical tolerance. We then price the attack: with eight target labels and 2,000 unlabelled calibration examples, a 10% mean relative feature edit yields 79.8% test accuracy, which is 91.2% of the fitted score's gain over chance; tighter edit limits sharply reduce success. Linear guardedness therefore remains a valid guarantee about the current representation, but it is not by itself a tamper-resistance guarantee for an editable open-weight model.

title: Improved Leverage Score Sampling for Constrained Active Linear Regression
abstract: In this paper we study active learning for constrained linear regression. Given a design matrix $A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times d}$, a constraint set $C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d$, and query access to $b\in\mathbb{R}^n$, we seek an approximate solution to $\min_{x\in C}\|Ax-b\|_2^2$ using as few queries as possible. This problem arises in many scientific and engineering applications, and randomized leverage score sampling provides a powerful method to solve it. However, existing leverage score methods ignore the constraint or encode it through ridge regularization, suffering unfavorable query complexity for anisotropic constraint sets. We propose ellipsoid-regularized leverage scores, where we approximate the constraint set by an outer ellipsoid and use its shape matrix to bias sampling toward directions that matter under the constraint geometry. We prove that the query complexity is governed by an anisotropic effective dimension $d_{\text{eff}}(C)\le d$. With appropriate parameters, $O(d_{\text{eff}}(C)\log d/\varepsilon^2)$ queries suffice to return a point in $C$ with objective value at most $(1+\varepsilon)$ times the optimum. This bound can substantially improve on the standard leverage-score bound, since anisotropic constraints can make $d_{\text{eff}}(C)$ much smaller than $d$. For convex constraints, we improve the dependence on $\varepsilon$ from $1/\varepsilon^2$ to $1/\varepsilon$. We also prove two lower bounds: first, the $d/\varepsilon^2$ dependence is unavoidable without convexity assumptions on $C$, and second, in some regimes, the effective dimension dependence $d_{\mathrm{eff}}(C)/\varepsilon$ is necessary for ellipsoidal constraints. Experiments on synthetic regression problems and a parametric heat conduction problem show lower regression error than standard baselines for similar query budget.

title: Toward Out-of-Distribution Generalization in Neural AC Power Flow
abstract: Growing uncertainty in power system operations from renewables integration, extreme weather, and data center loads challenges the reliability of traditional power flow solvers at scale. Machine learning-based proxies are a potentially promising alternative, but the prohibitive cost of generating training data for large grids makes out-of-distribution generalization a key capability for deployment; currently, models trained on small grids lack that capability. In this work, we systematically evaluate how physics-informed losses, multi-grid training, and perturbation-based data augmentation improve the zero-shot transfer of three graph neural network-based power flow models from smaller systems to a larger, unseen 500-bus system. We find that (1) physics-informed losses improve transfer relative to purely supervised objectives; (2) multi-grid training on smaller systems matches the best single grid but does not close the gap to target-grid training; (3) perturbation-based augmentation on edge attributes improves transfer by up to 54.6%; and (4) random line/generator dropout does not consistently improve performance.

title: Do 3D Point Representations Encode Architectural Functions? Probing Supervised and Pretrained Models on Urban Facades
abstract: Semantic labels say what a building element is, not what it does: two identical-looking windows on one facade may be operable or fixed, a column may carry load or only decorate. We ask whether 3D point representations encode such architectural function. On 22 mobile-LiDAR buildings with 15 functional attributes per element, we hold out entire buildings and compare hand-crafted descriptors, networks trained from scratch and frozen self-supervised point transformers. Descriptors and frozen features are read by the same linear layer. No network trained from scratch, from PointNet to a 108M-parameter PTv3, clearly exceeds the descriptors (0.610 mAP on functionally ambiguous elements), whereas frozen Utonia reaches 0.732. Random-weight controls of the same architectures (0.649 and 0.652) attribute the gain to pretraining (Utonia: +0.080, 95% building interval [+0.035, +0.124]). Pretrained features improve at every tested number of labelled buildings while descriptors and random features plateau, and, in the configurations we tested, fine-tuning erodes the benefit: at today's data scale, function is better read from pretrained representations than learned from scratch.

title: MoMoVL: Modality-Aware Adaptive Compression for On-Device Sparsely-Activated Vision-Language Models
abstract: The rise of the agentic web has been accompanied by growing demand for on-device Vision-Language Models (VLMs) that perform diverse cross-modal web tasks with enhanced privacy and reduced latency. Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models are widely adopted in modern VLMs for compute-efficient scalability, yet their multi-expert architecture poses deployment challenges due to substantial memory demands. Mixed-precision quantization is an effective compression technique that reduces bit-widths while adapting to the heterogeneous hardware budgets of edge devices, particularly well-suited for MoE due to its inherent structural sparsity, which causes imbalanced importance among experts. While prior work has applied quantization for efficient MoE inference at the edge, we point out that in MoE-based VLMs, the modality-specific characteristics of visual and text tokens further impact expert quantization. To address this issue, we present MoMoVL, a modality-aware adaptive compression framework for MoE-based VLMs that brings vision-language inference within reach of on-device resource budgets. Motivated by our empirical findings on modality-induced disparities across experts, MoMoVL jointly exploits the per-expert activation profile and per-modality quantization sensitivity to guide bit-width assignment. Experimental results show that MoMoVL improves the accuracy-compression trade-off relative to state-of-the-art mixed-precision baselines and reduces memory footprint by up to 15.44% with a modest drop in accuracy over its uniform-precision baseline. Our code and data are publicly available at https://github.com/sco-edge/MoMoVL.

title: Evaluating Governed LLM-Driven ML Experimentation: Lifecycle, Provenance, and Failure Metrics
abstract: Autonomous agents that run ML experiments are usually judged by the best score they reach. That score says nothing about how it was reached: whether the agent stayed within the files it was allowed to edit, whether failed trials were kept or silently dropped, and whether each keep or discard decision can be traced to its evidence. We propose evaluating such systems on their experimental process as well as their outcome, and we build a governed harness that makes this possible. A control plane, not the LLM that proposes changes, owns each trial's lifecycle, checks its edit scope, decides keep or discard, and appends one record per trial to an append-only ledger. Governance metrics such as the invalid-action rate, the repeated-bad rate and provenance completeness are computed from that ledger. Across six ML tasks, from synthetic logistic regression to language-model training, and 1,445 trials, the same contract applied unchanged. The ledger exposed failures that a task score hides: a no-memory arm in which all 120 trials failed, a benchmark adapter whose bounded proposals ran out, and a reset failure that reproducibility hashes revealed, after which the affected campaigns were rerun. In a matched counterfactual, a loop that logs only successful trials left no record of 43 of 50 trials, while the governed ledger recorded all 50. Memory ablations show that memory's effect on repeated bad proposals depends on the task. We release the ledgers of all 1,445 trials, so that every number reported for them can be recomputed.

title: Agent Verifiers in Counterfactual Analysis: A Pilot Study Benchmarking Agentic Heterogeneous Treatment Effects
abstract: Agents can expand the covariate space of randomized experiments by retrieving fast-moving local context missed by slow-changing survey baseline covariates, helping characterize who benefits most from an intervention. Verifying such covariates is difficult: individual treatment effects are unobserved, retrieval leakage can pull post-treatment information into nominally pretreatment summaries, and encoder leakage can inject post-treatment pretraining knowledge into representations even after temporal filtering of inputs. Guided by a two-channel information bound separating summary provenance from encoder weights, we propose a three-layer benchmark protocol: (i) retrieval admissibility via pre-treatment date filtering; (ii) heterogeneity validation scored rank-weighted average treatment effects (RATEs); and (iii) encoder admissibility checked with chronologically vintaged encoders, future-fact probes, and weight perturbations. Across 11 datasets anchored by Uganda's Youth Opportunities Program, we compare session-isolated retrieval (sandboxed, bounded-budget agent runs per study) against a persistent workspace teammate (xAI's GrokBot) that builds one date-verified corpus per study while blinded to outcomes. The workspace teammate yields higher mean RATE ratios in 6/11 datasets for text alone and 7 for combined features, though paired tests show neither workflow universally dominates. Even on fixed retrieved text, encoder choice significantly shifts heterogeneity signal. Chronologically vintaged probes show no clear evidence of weight leakage, but single-record adapter perturbation analyses show that memorized future facts, once present, persist until injected noise degrades model output. Temporal filtering of retrieval is necessary but insufficient: verifying agent-generated covariates requires jointly examining source provenance, out-of-sample treatment-effect signal, and encoder weights.

title: Label-Free Role-Aware Segmentation of Classroom Recordings: Recovering the Teacher from Transferable Structure
abstract: How much the teacher talks and when are among the most informative and costly-to-measure signals of teaching. Yet, classroom audio is among the most sensitive data an AI system can process: recordings capture minors and fall under GDPR, preventing raw audio from leaving the recording device. We present a teacher-student segmentation pipeline designed to meet exactly this constraint: label-free at inference, running on a recording device, and requiring no per-session calibration.
